You necrotize part of a creature's body, harming them and debilitating them as their body putrefies, mimicking the natural process of decay. The target takes 12d6 void damage and one of the following debilitations; roll 1d4 to randomly determine which. The effects depend on their Fortitude save.1 Bones The target's bones necrotize and become spongy and weak, giving them weakness 3 to bludgeoning damage.2 Joints The target's joints necrotize and become frail, making their movements ungainly and clumsy. They become clumsy 1.3 Legs The target's legs (or any other limbs associated with forms of movement) necrotize, making it harder for the creature to move. The target takes a –10-foot status penalty to their Speeds.4 Muscles The target's muscles necrotize, rotting away. The target becomes enfeebled 1.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target takes half damage, and the debilitation lasts until the end of your next turn.

Failure The target takes full damage, and the debilitation lasts for 1 minute.

Critical Failure The target takes double damage, and you can pick a second debilitation to apply, in addition to the one you rolled randomly. Both debilitations last for 1 minute.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 2d6.

name: Nudge the Odds
description:
You bestow yourself supernaturally good luck at cards, dice, and other games of chance. You gain a +1 status bonus to Games Lore checks to gamble, and if you roll a critical failure on such a check, you get a failure instead; however, the spell is too short-lived to use for Earn Income checks from gambling. When you're under the effect of nudge the odds, one facial feature, such as a lock of hair or the iris of an eye, transforms to a distinctive golden color; the GM chooses which feature when you Cast the Spell. This change resists all magical efforts to conceal it, though it can be hidden or covered by mundane means. A creature noticing the feature can identify the spell using Recall Knowledge. Because it prevents losing big, gamblers consider nudge the odds a repugnant form of cheating. If you're caught using the spell, you're likely to suffer serious consequences depending on the nature of the gamblers you cheated.

Heightened (5th) The status bonus increases to +2, and the duration increases to lasting until the next time you make your daily preparations. If you continue spending your spell slot each day to keep the duration active, this allows you to apply the effect to a downtime check to Earn Income.

name: Nullify
description: You instantly destroy the incoming spell, though at the cost of sending magical feedback through your body. You automatically counteract the spell, but the feedback brings you unavoidable harm. You lose 1d8 Hit Points per rank of the triggering spell.

name: One with the Land
description: You merge with an adjacent natural feature with enough volume to fit you and your worn and held possessions, such as the ground or a large tree. Your merged form is visible within the feature, and creatures can target and attack you normally, though you have cover and can use it to Hide or Take Cover within the feature. You can cast spells while in the feature as long as they don’t require line of effect beyond the feature. You can Dismiss the spell. While merged, you gain the following additional benefits. You immediately become aware of the surrounding terrain features, and you gain tremorsense as an imprecise sense with a range of 200 feet.You can make terrain vengeance Strikes by commanding plants, rocks, and other natural features to attack your foes. These are melee Strikes that use your spell attack modifier, can target any creature within 60 feet of you, and deal 5d12 bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage. You choose the damage type each time you make a terrain vengeance Strike.By spending a single action, which has the concentrate trait, you can increase or decrease the environmental temperature, changing it to either one step warmer than normal, one step colder than normal, or the normal temperature.As a 2-action activity that has the concentrate trait, you can create or remove difficult terrain caused by natural terrain in a 20-foot burst within 200 feet. All your alterations to the land end when the spell ends. Significant physical damage to the natural feature while you are inside it expels you and deals 10d6 damage to you.

name: Overload Connection
description:
Typically, the connection between a familiar and its master carries subtle mental magic only felt between the two. Some casters learn to empower this magic, blasting scrambled lines of their mental conversations to any target between them. When you Cast this Spell and the first time you Sustain this spell on subsequent turns, this magical connection flares in a line between you and your familiar, dealing 3d8 mental damage to all creatures in the line, with a basic Reflex save.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d8.

name: Painful Vibrations
description:
You send powerful sound waves through an opponent’s body, vibrating its bones and internal organs painfully. The creature takes 8d6 sonic damage and must attempt a Fortitude save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target takes half damage.

Failure The target takes full damage, is sickened 1, and is deafened for 1 round.

Critical Failure The target takes double damage, is sickened 2, and is deafened for 1 minute.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 2d6.

name: Palm-Held Sun
description: You open a rift into Creation’s Forge, igniting it into a miniature star that blazes with mighty light. You shed bright light in a 30-foot emanation (and dim light to the next 30 feet). When you Cast or Sustain the spell, each creature with void healing in the aura takes 1 vitality damage, and any creature in the aura with a particular vulnerability to sunlight becomes slowed 1 for 1 round unless it succeeds at a Fortitude save. After a creature in the aura loses HP due to fire damage from any source, it takes 1 vitality damage.

name: Patron's Protector
description:
You channel your magic into your familiar, filling its body with dreadful energy, turning them into a powerful protective force. You can use Command an Animal on the target as part of Casting or Sustaining this spell. Your familiar's AC becomes 28; they become large, and they gain 20 temporary Hit Points. If your familiar is reduced to 0 Hit Points while under the effect of this spell, the spell immediately ends, and your familiar is instead reduced to 1 Hit Point. Once per turn your familiar can use the Body Check or Protector's Shove action.

Body Check [single action] Your familiar uses its new size and presence to press against an adjacent creature, dealing, 4d10 bludgeoning damage (basic Fortitude save). On a failed save, the target is also knocked back 10 feet (20 feet on a critical failure).

Protector's Shove [single action] Your familiar shoves an ally out of danger. Your familiar pushes an adjacent, willing ally, pushing them up to 20 feet away and granting them a +2 status bonus to AC for 1 round. This is forced movement.

Heightened (9th) The familiar’s AC become 36, they gain 30 temporary Hit Points, and the damage increases by 2d10.

name: Perfected Thrall
description: You create a perfect thrall that’s the conglomeration of all aspects of necromancy. The perfected thrall is made of pure, dense muscle, covered in a layer of hardened bone, and inhabited by the spirit of a mighty warrior. It wields a weapon made of blood that forms into the ideal weapon for any situation before becoming harder than iron. You create a thrall that has 200 Hit Points and a Speed of 40 feet. Whenever you use an ability that would destroy this thrall, it instead loses 20 Hit Points. The spirit inhabiting this thrall can inspire other spirits to join the fray with their inspiring attacks. Whenever the perfected thrall critically hits a creature, you create up to 4 thralls, each of which must be adjacent to either the perfected thrall or the Strike’s target. When you use thrall charge to order this thrall to Strike, the Strike deals an additional 6d6 damage.

name: Pernicious Poltergeist
description:
You create an echo of a powerful poltergeist, temporarily anchoring it to the area. Because the poltergeist is a manifestation and not truly present, it can’t be attacked or hurt; it remains invisible unless otherwise stated. When you Cast the Spell, and the first time you Sustain it on subsequent rounds, the poltergeist creates your choice of one of the following effects.

  • Deathly Assault (void) The poltergeist focuses on one creature in the area and flies through that creature, dealing 4d10 void damage with a basic Fortitude save.
  • Frighten (emotion, fear, mental) The poltergeist becomes visible, appearing as a skeletal, ghostlike humanoid. Creatures in the area must attempt a Will save, becoming frightened 2 on a failure.
  • Telekinetic Storm (force) The poltergeist hurls debris and quasi-real objects around in the area. All creatures in the area take 4d8 force damage with a basic Reflex save.

Heightened (+2) The damage of the deathly assault effect increases by 1d10, and the damage of the telekinetic storm effect increases by 1d8.

name: Persistent Servant
description: You call forth a phantasmal minion and task it to perform a specific chore repeatedly. Choose a basic instruction, such as sweeping the floor or picking up all objects from the floor and putting them in a designated bin. The servant performs the task over and over again throughout the duration, though it can't ever leave the spell's area. The servant isn't a minion, and you don't need to Sustain the Spell in order for it to continue to act. However, it acts on its own time, and thus can't accomplish anything useful during an encounter, even if an encounter happens within the spell's range. Tasks that rely on timing, discretion, or significant manual dexterity are doomed to failure. For instance, a servant tasked to pick objects off the floor won't discriminate between trash, misplaced treasure, or objects that are supposed to be on the floor, like a mousetrap.

name: Petal Storm
description:
You bring forth a cloud of razor-sharp flower petals that thrash violently in the wind. A creature that enters the storm or starts its turn in the storm is sliced by the razor-sharp edges of the petals. It takes 2d10 slashing damage with a basic Reflex save. A creature can take damage from the petals only once per round. At the end of the duration, the storm calms and the petals fall harmlessly to the ground.

Heightened (+2) The damage increases by 1d10.

name: Phantom Crowd
description:
A tightly packed crowd of humanoids appropriate to the area appear, facing you and agreeing loudly with anything you say. A creature that touches a member of the crowd or attempts a Seek action to examine the crowd can attempt to disbelieve your illusion. The crowd is difficult terrain for anyone who hasn’t disbelieved the illusion. When you spend 1 or more actions to cast a composition spell or to perform an activity that includes a Performance check, you can also Sustain this Spell as part of that action.

Heightened (+1) The crowd occupies an additional 10-foot-by-10-foot square in range. The additional square doesn’t need to be adjacent to any other square. It can overlap, but there’s no additional effect in the overlapped squares.

name: Phantom Prison
description:
You completely surround a Large or smaller creature in immobile illusory walls, trapping it inside a false prison it can’t escape. No other creatures see or feel these walls, and the target can’t see anything outside of the illusory walls. The target can attempt a Will save when the spell is cast, each time it attempts to interact with or escape the walls, and each time something from outside the walls affects the target. On a success, it disbelieves the illusion, and the spell ends.

Heightened (8th) You can target up to five creatures.

name: Pierce the Sky
description:
You summon a bow and launch up to three arrow-shaped thunderbolts that scream through the air and can be heard from a mile away. Make a ranged spell attack roll against each target. Each attack counts toward your multiple attack penalty, but you don't increase your penalty until you've made all your attacks. Each arrow deals 6d12 electricity damage and 6d6 sonic damage. Regardless of the result, each arrow leaves a line of hazardous terrain between you and the target that lasts for 1 minute. A creature that enters or starts its turn in the hazardous terrain takes 12 electricity damage; a creature can only be damaged by this hazardous terrain once per round.

Critical Success The target takes double damage and is deafened for 1 minute.

Success The target takes full damage and is deafened for 1 round.

Failure The target takes half damage.

Critical Failure The target is unaffected.

name: Planar Collision
description:
You rip out a portion of an elemental plane and smash it into your plane, unleashing a chaotic maelstrom. When you Cast this Spell, choose an elemental plane. The collision deals 8d6 force damage and 8d8 damage of a type depending on the chosen plane to each creature in the area with a basic Reflex save. A creature that fails the saving throw is also pushed 25 feet away from the center of the burst (or 50 feet on a critical failure). Each creature whose movement is stopped by a firm surface, such as a well, takes bludgeoning damage equal to the remaining number of feet it would've moved. The area also becomes difficult terrain and hazardous terrain that lasts for a year and a day or until counteracted by a spell or effect such as dispel magic. Any creature that ends its turn in the hazardous terrain takes 15 damage of a type depending on the chosen plane.

  • Plane of Air The damage dealt is acid damage, and the spell gains the air trait.
  • Plane of Earth The damage dealt is bludgeoning damage, and the spell gains the earth trait.
  • Plane of Fire The damage dealt is fire damage, and the spell gains the fire trait.
  • Plane of Metal The damage dealt is slashing damage, and the spell gains the metal trait.
  • Plane of Water The damage dealt is cold damage, and the spell gains the water trait.
  • Plane of Wood The damage dealt is piercing damage, and the spell gains the wood trait.

name: Plasma Whirl
description:
You reach up to the stars and create a temporary portal that allows a blast of plasma to pass through the battlefield. The plasma deals electricity and fire damage with a basic Reflex save. The number of actions you spend when Casting this Spell determines the area and other parameters.

[single action] This spell is a 15-foot cone, dealing 2d6 electricity damage and 2d6 fire damage. [two actions] This spell is a 30-foot cone, dealing 5d6 electricity damage and 5d6 fire damage. [three actions] This spell is a 60-foot cone, dealing 5d6 electricity damage and 5d6 fire damage. Creatures that fail their saves become sickened 1 (sickened 2 on a critical failure) due to their exposure to cosmic radiation.

Heightened (+2) The damage increases by 1d6 for each damage type with the 1-action version, or by 2d6 for each damage type for the 2-and 3-action versions.

name: Propelling Air Stream
duration: until the end of your next turn
description:
You shoot out a high-speed blast of air that propels you into the air. Make a ranged spell attack against a target’s AC. On a success, the target takes 2d6 bludgeoning damage (or double damage on a critical hit). Regardless of whether you hit, you gain a fly Speed of 15 feet until the end of your next turn.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 2d6.

name: Protect Companion
target: your eidolon, or a creature with the minion trait under your control
duration: until the start of your next turn
description:
You extend your aura as a magical shield that protects your eidolon or minion. The target gains a +1 circumstance bonus to AC until the start of your next turn. You gain the following reaction; after using the reaction, the spell ends and you can't cast protect companion again for 10 minutes.

Life Block [reaction] Trigger The spell's target would take damage;Effect Reduce the triggering damage by 10, but you lose 5 Hit Points. Even if this reduces the damage to 0, the target still takes any effects that would come with the damage, such as the poison on a viper's fangs Strike.

Heightened (+2) The reaction reduces the damage by another 10, and you lose 5 more Hit Points. If you want to lose fewer Hit Points, you can choose to lower the damage reduction and HP lost to what any lower-rank version of the spell could do without lowering the spell’s actual rank.

name: Proximal Shift
description: With a thunderous crack, you disappear from your current location and reappear in an unoccupied space within range that you can see, bringing all non-magical, non-living, unattended matter (including objects) in a 5-foot emanation with you. Creatures within the emanation must succeed at a Reflex save to avoid falling into the crater you leave behind, taking 5 bludgeoning damage and falling prone. Creatures in a 5-foot emanation on your arrival space take 6d6 bludgeoning damage with a basic Reflex save from the resulting explosion of debris, and the area becomes difficult terrain for 1 minute. At the GM's discretion, the spell might have additional effects based on the nature of the material teleported with you. If the teleport would cause you to bring another creature—even one inside an extradimensional container—the spell fails.

name: Psychic Outburst
description:
Psychic energy filters through your mind and explodes outward, dealing mental damage to creatures in the area with a basic Will save. The number of actions you spend when Casting this Spell determines the damage and other parameters.

[two actions] The spell deals 6d10 mental damage. [three actions] The spell deals 6d10 mental damage. Creatures that fail their save are pushed 10 feet away from you (or 20 feet on a critical failure). Two Rounds If you spend 3 actions Casting the Spell, you can avoid finishing the spell and spend another 2 actions on your next turn to empower the spell even further. You can take other actions before finishing this spell, but the spell is lost if you Cast another Spell in between. The area increases to a 40-foot emanation, deals 8d10 mental damage, and targets only enemies. Creatures that fail their save are pushed 10 feet away from you (20 feet on a critical failure).

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d10.

name: Puppet Strings
description:
Ethereal threads emanate from your fingertips and flow toward the target, connecting to its arms, legs, and body. The target must attempt a Reflex save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The strings impede the target's movements, but you can't control them. The target is clumsy 1 until the end of its next turn.

Failure The target is clumsy 1 and slowed 1. Additionally, when you Cast this Spell and the first time you Sustain it on subsequent turns, you can force the target to Stride or Strike. If you force the target to Stride, you determine the path it takes; you can't force it to Stride into a space where it can't stand easily. This is forced movement. If you cause the creature to Strike, it makes a melee Strike against a creature within its reach using your spell attack modifier. The target can't hit itself this way. On a hit, the Strike deals 7d6 bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage, as appropriate. None of the target's equipment or abilities modify this Strike. This Strike contributes to and uses your multiple attack penalty. At the end of its turn, the target can attempt a Fortitude save against your spell DC to free itself from the threads. On a success, the spell ends.

Critical Failure As failure, but the target is slowed 2, and you can force the target to use 2 actions when you Cast or Sustain the spell.

name: Pyroclastic Truth
description:
This impossible spell is more devious and insistent than most. While all impossible spells long to be used, this spell relentlessly urges those who learn it to destroy everything in their path. The blast of liquid fire created by this spell brands the soul of those who are touched by its flames, dealing 2d12 fire damage to all creatures, structures, and unattended objects in the area. All creatures damaged by this spell are marked by fire for the duration of the spell. When you Fuel Pyroclastic Truth, all creatures marked by fire take 1d12 persistent fire damage.

Lethologic Mark You understand the true desire of fire to burn away your soul. Whenever you take fire damage, you become frightened 1. Additionally, if you're reduced to 0 Hit Points by a fire effect, you instantly die and are turned to ash, and your soul is cast into the Plane of Fire to burn for eternity. To heal this mark, you must perform an atone ritual in both the Plane of Fire and the Plane of Water.

Heightened (+1) The initial fire damage increases by 2d12, and the persistent fire damage increases by 1d12.

name: Quantic Dampening
description:
You demonstrate exceptional control over elemental forces, allowing you to mitigate the effects of energy damage. As a reaction, whenever you or an ally in the area would attempt a basic Reflex save to resist an effect that deals acid, cold, electricity, fire, force, or sonic damage, they use the outcome one degree of success better than the result of their saving throw.

Heightened (8th) The area increases to a 30-foot emanation.

name: Quick Sort
target: up to 200 unattended objects in range, each of light Bulk or less
description:
You magically sort a group of objects into neat stacks or piles. You can sort the objects in two different ways. The first option is to separate them into different piles depending on an easily observed factor, such as color or shape. Alternatively, you can sort the objects into ordered stacks depending on a clearly indicated notation, such as a page number, title, or date. The objects sort themselves throughout the duration, though it takes less time per object to sort a smaller number of objects, down to a single round for 30 or fewer objects.

Heightened (3rd) The spell can sort up to 500 objects in a minute, or 75 objects in a round.

name: Read the Air
description: You survey a social situation, showing courtesy to all around you as your intuition swiftly picks up clues about social contexts and unspoken assumptions of behavior. Your body language subconsciously changes to take advantage of this information and use it in your own interactions with those creatures. As part of Casting this Spell, you Recall Knowledge using Society to gain information about the social situation. You also gain a +1 status bonus to your next Diplomacy check to Make an Impression on those creatures present when you Cast this Spell, as long as the check occurs during the duration of the spell. You can read the air only once in a given social situation; casting it again has no effect.

name: Reanimate Foe
description:
You launch a thrall up to 30 feet into the corpse of an enemy that has been dead for no more than 1 minute, destroying the thrall in an effort to call the corpse to fight. Attempt an Undead Lore check against the standard DC of the level of enemy you’re trying to reanimate. You can reanimate only corpses of creatures that were once living or undead.

Success The enemy reanimates in an unoccupied space adjacent to its corpse. It’s under your control and has the minion trait. It has the same attack modifier, AC, saving throw modifiers, Perception, and skill modifiers, but it has only 100 Hit Points and lacks all special abilities, including immunities, resistances, and weaknesses. It has no magic items except the weapons and armor it used before death. Its Strikes deal the normal damage but don’t apply added effects since the creature doesn’t have special abilities. The reanimated foe is unstable and decays quickly. Each turn after it takes its actions, it loses 15 Hit Points. It can’t regain its lost Hit Points in any way. The reanimated creature lasts for 1 minute or until it’s reduced to 0 Hit Points.

Failure As success, but the reanimated enemy deals half damage with its Strikes and loses 50 Hit Points each turn instead of 15.

Critical Failure You create a thrall in the corpse’s space, but you don’t spend the Focus Point for casting this spell.

name: Reblooded
description:
Your enemy’s heart has been stopped, but you cause it to start pumping blood once again. The unfamiliar sensation is enough to throw the creature off-kilter, while the blood itself damages the flesh of the undead. The target attempts a Fortitude save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes 1d6 persistent acid damage.

Failure The creature is clumsy 1 for 1 minute and takes 2d6 persistent acid damage.

Critical Failure The creature is clumsy 2 for 1 minute and takes 3d6 persistent acid damage.

name: Recurring Nightmare
description:
You conjure forth a ghostly thrall that isn’t easily slain. You create a thrall within range, and you can create it in a space occupied by a creature. Unlike other thralls, the nightmare can share its space with other creatures, and other creatures can move through its space with ease. If this thrall is summoned into or ends its movement in a creature’s space, the creature must succeed at a Will saving throw or become frightened 1 (or frightened 2 on a critical failure); this is an emotion, fear, and mental effect. The thrall has a fly Speed of 60 feet and remains airborne at the end of your turn even if it didn’t Fly that turn. Any ability you use that would make the thrall Stride allows it to Fly instead. The thrall’s Strikes deal void damage and must target a creature in the thrall’s space. When you use thrall charge to order this thrall to make a Strike, that Strike deals an additional 2d6 damage. If the thrall has been destroyed, you can Sustain this spell to resummon the thrall. You can do this only once per round.

Heightened (8th) The additional damage increases to 3d6.

name: Reinforce Eidolon
description:
You focus deeply on the link between you and your eidolon and reinforce your eidolon’s defenses. Your eidolon gains a +1 status bonus to AC and saving throws, plus resistance 1 to all damage equal to half the spell’s rank (minimum 1).

Special Your eidolon can benefit from either boost eidolon or reinforce eidolon, but not both; if you cast one of these spells during the other's duration, the newer spell replaces the older one.

name: Remake Physiology
description:
At your touch, the target's body shifts and transmutes into random mismatched animal parts, such as crab claws for hands and mismatched gazelle and gorilla legs. The target must attempt a Fortitude save. Due to the unbalanced body weight and mismatched limbs, the target takes a –20-foot status penalty to its Speeds.The creature's mind and body no longer align, making it clumsy 1, drained 1, enfeebled 1, and stupefied 1.The target's new eyes make depth perception difficult; the target becomes dazzled.Whenever the target would regain actions at the start of its turn, it must first attempt a DC 5 flat check; on a failure, it's slowed 1 for a round.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is affected for 1 round.

Failure The target is affected for 1 minute.

Critical Failure The effect is permanent.

name: Rend Magic
description:
You spew forth pure magical energy down your arm before releasing it in a devastating attack. Make a melee spell attack against the target’s AC. If it hits, the target takes 3d10 force damage, then takes 1d10 force damage each time it Casts a Spell for 1 minute; on a critical hit, double the initial damage and the damage when the target casts spells. This spell ends immediately if the target ends its turn without Casting a Spell.

Heightened (+2) The initial force damage increases by 2d10, and the force damage taken whenever the target casts a spell increases by 1d10.

name: Restraining Chains
target: 1 creature touching or standing on a solid surface
description:
A steel chain materializes from the surface, fettered to one space of your choice that the target occupies, weaving itself around the creature’s limbs. The chain continuously pulls on the target and impedes its movement. The chain has AC 10, Hardness 5, and 30 Hit Points, and it’s immune to critical hits and precision damage.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target can only move up to 20 feet away from where the chains are fettered until the chains are broken or the target Escapes.

Failure The target is clumsy 1 and can only move up to 10 feet away from where the chains are fettered until the chains are broken or the target Escapes.

Critical Failure The chain binds the target tighter. The target is clumsy 2 and can only move up to 5 feet away from where the chains are fettered until the chains are broken or the target Escapes.

name: Restyle
target: 1 piece of clothing currently worn by you or an ally
description: You permanently change the appearance of one piece of clothing currently worn by you or an ally to better fit your aesthetic sensibilities. You can change its color, texture, pattern, and other minor parts of its design, but the changes can’t alter the clothing’s overall shape, size, or purpose. The changes can’t increase the quality of the craftsmanship or artistry of the piece of clothing, but particularly gauche choices for the new color and pattern might decrease its aesthetic appeal. This spell transforms existing materials into the desired appearance and never alters the material or creates more material than what’s originally part of the object. The object’s statistics also remain unchanged.

name: Retrieving Hook
target: 1 creature or an unattended object of 2 Bulk or less
description:
You conjure a magical hook and rope that hurtles toward the target and pulls them to you. The target must attempt a Fortitude save. If the target is a willing ally or unattended object, they automatically fail the save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is pulled 5 feet toward you.

Failure The target is pulled to the nearest empty space adjacent to you.

Critical Failure As failure, and the target is off-guard for 1 round.

Heightened (5th) The range increases to 30 feet.

name: Rewinding Step
description:
You anchor your location in time so that you can swiftly retrace your steps later with complex chronomancy. The space you’re in when you Cast the Spell becomes your temporal anchor space. While you’re within 500 feet of your temporal anchor space, you can Sustain this spell to instantaneously return to that space (you don’t need to have line of effect). The spell then ends. You bring any items that are in your possession with you when you take the action to return.

If the anchor space is occupied when you attempt to return to it or if this spell would bring another creature with you, the spell fails to transport you, then ends.

Heightened (7th) You can return if you’re within 1,000 feet of your anchor space.

Heightened (9th) You can return if you’re within 1 mile of your anchor space.

name: Rip the Spirit
description:
You supernaturally rip the spirit from a living creature’s body, dooming the target to pain and death. The target takes 5d6 void damage, depending on its basic Fortitude save, and is also drained 1 if it fails its save. The spell’s effect is based on how many actions you spend when Casting the Spell. [single action] The spell targets one living creature in range. [two actions] (concentrate) The spell targets one living creature in range, and the damage is 10d6 void damage instead of 5d6. [three actions] (concentrate) The spell targets all living creatures in a 30-foot emanation.

Heightened (+1) The amount of damage increases by 1d6, or by 2d6 for the 2-action version.

name: Roaring Applause
description:
Your flamboyant flourish invokes such powerful feelings in your audience that you incite cheers and applause. The target of this spell must be able to see, hear, or otherwise understand you. The target must attempt a Will save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target becomes mildly distracted and applauds while it isn’t fully occupied. It can’t use reactions.

Failure The target applauds you so vigorously that it can’t use reactions and is slowed 1. The applause is so involved that it has the manipulate trait. This triggers reactions based on the manipulate trait at the start of the target’s turn.

Critical Failure As failure, plus the target is so distracted by its vigorous applauding of you that it’s fascinated with you.

Heightened (6th) You can target up to 10 creatures.

name: Runic Impression
target: you or one weapon you’re wielding
description:
Your unarmed attacks or your weapon gain the benefits of a weapon rune you choose when you cast this spell: corrosive, flaming, frost, ghost touch, returning, shock, or thundering. If you cast runic impression on a weapon, this spell ends if you cease holding the weapon, with the exception of throwing a returning weapon.

If this spell would give a weapon more property runes than its normal maximum, one of the existing property runes (your choice) is suppressed until the spell ends. For unarmed attacks, if this spell would give you more property runes than you could have from handwraps of mighty blows, one of the existing property runes is similarly suppressed.

Heightened (8th) Add keen to the list of runes you can choose as well as the greater versions of corrosive, flaming, frost, shock, and thundering.

name: Sacred Covenant
target: you and up to 5 willing creatures
description: You and your allies make a sacred pact with each other, ensuring that no matter what happens, your quest will be complete. All creatures are bound by your deity’s edicts and anathema. Violating an anathema ends the spell effect on the creature that committed the anathema, but nobody else. When a target would be reduced to 0 Hit Points but not immediately killed, it avoids being knocked out and continues to fight. It remains at 1 Hit Point, gains 50 temporary Hit Points that last for 1 minute, and increases its wounded condition by 1. Each target can only avoid being knocked out in this way once, then becomes immune to sacred covenant until its next daily preparations.

name: Sanguine Mist
description:
You create a cloud of bloodsucking fog that drains the life from the living. Each living creature in the area when you Cast the Spell, aside from you, takes 6d6 void damage with a basic Fortitude save. Creatures in the area are concealed, and all creatures outside the cloud become concealed to creatures within it.

The first time each round you Sustain this spell on subsequent turns, living creatures in the area take an additional 2d6 void damage with another basic Fortitude save. You also gain temporary Hit Points equal to half the damage a single creature took when you Sustained the spell this turn; calculate these temporary Hit Points using the creature that took the most damage. These temporary Hit Points last for 1 minute.

Heightened (+1) The initial damage increases by 2d6, and the secondary damage increases by 1d6.

name: Sanguine Transference
description: You diffuse your spirit into your blood before escaping your body and transferring your blood and soul into a thrall. You use the target thrall to reform your body in its space, and you leave a thrall where your body once was. Your reformed body is the same as it was before the transfer. All spells and effects applied to you remain active. Tendrils of blood grab all your items as you travel and equip them to your new body as they were before the transfer. The movement of your blood doesn’t trigger any reactions.

name: Seashell of Stolen Sound
description:
You store a sound in a seashell to use as you will: the last words of a loved one, a dragon’s mighty roar, the compromising conversation between two powerful diplomats, or even something stranger and secret. As part of Casting this Spell, you must present an unbroken seashell. When you Cast the Spell, magic swirls around the triggering creature, copying the sounds it makes, as well as any background noise, for the next minute and storing them in the seashell.

You or another creature can then play the sound back from the seashell during the spell’s duration by Interacting with the seashell, but once the sounds have been played back, the seashell shatters, and the spell ends.

As normal for spells with a duration until your next daily preparations, you can choose to continue expending the spell slot to prolong the duration of an existing seashell of stolen sound for another day. While the spell faithfully copies the sounds around the target, it doesn’t reproduce any special auditory or sonic effects of the sound.

name: Shadow Army
description:
You create dozens of semi-real copies of yourself that swarm across the battlefield and fight your enemies. You’re virtually indistinguishable from your clones, allowing you to Hide and Sneak among them. An enemy that’s in the area when the spell is cast or that ends their turn in the area takes 3d10 mental damage and 3d10 bludgeoning damage, and is possibly inflicted with a condition, depending on the result of their Will save. When you Cast the Spell, you choose a condition your shadows impose on a failed save: clumsy 2, enfeebled 2, off-guard, or slowed 1.

Critical Success The creature takes no damage. For the duration of the spell, the creature uses the outcome one degree of success better than it rolled on further saves against the spell and can distinguish you from your clones without difficulty.

Success The creature takes half damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage and gains the chosen condition until the end of its next turn.

Critical Failure The creature takes double damage and gains the chosen condition until the end of its next turn.

name: Shadow Projectile
description:
You create an illusory duplicate of your ally’s ranged attack. You launch an illusory double of your ally’s projectile or spell at the same target, leaving the enemy unsure which attack to avoid. The target takes 3d8 mental damage, depending on its Will save. Regardless of the result of its save, it’s temporarily immune to shadow projectile for 1 hour.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature is off-guard against the triggering attack.

Failure The creature is off-guard against the triggering attack and takes full damage from your illusory projectile.

Critical Failure As failure, but double damage.

Heightened (+2) The damage increases by 1d8.

name: Shadow Raid
description:
You spin illusions of flying shadows throughout the area. Enemies in the area when you Cast the Spell take 6d8 bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage, with a basic Reflex or Will save, as shadows explode into being. You choose the damage type when you Cast the Spell, and each creature chooses the type of save it attempts before it rolls the save. The shadows then persist in the area for 1 minute, dealing 3d8 damage of the type you chose to any enemy that ends their turn in the area. All creatures are concealed to enemies in the area, as the illusory shadows swarm over them and block light.

A creature that spends an action to Seek or otherwise interact with the shadow raid can attempt a Perception check to disbelieve it. On a success, the creature halves the damage it takes from the shadows, and the shadows no longer impede its vision. These benefits last until the spell ends.

Heightened (9th) The initial damage increases by 2d8, and the damage to a creature that ends its turn in the area increases by 1d8.

name: Shadow Strike
description:
You launch out a tendril of darkness that latches onto a target and pulls them toward you. Make a ranged spell attack against the target’s AC. On a hit, you deal 5d10 void damage, and the target is pulled up to 10 feet toward you. On a critical hit, you deal double the damage, and the target is pulled up to 20 feet toward you.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d10.

name: Shielding Strike
description: As you attack a foe, warding magic transforms your momentum into action and lifts your shield. You can either Raise your Shield if you’re wielding one or cast shield if you have the spell. Then, make a melee Strike.

name: Shift Perspective
description: You throw one item of light Bulk or less that you’re holding to a location within range that you can see, then gain temporary vision from where that object lands. The object sees in all directions with your normal visual senses. You can Sustain this spell to switch between the thrown object’s perspective and your regular vision while the spell is active, but you can only see through one perspective at a time. You can Dismiss this spell.

name: Shooting Star
description: You let loose a projectile that flies true and leaves the blazing trail of a meteor behind it. Make a ranged Strike, ignoring the target’s concealment and reducing the target’s cover by one degree for only this Strike (greater to standard, standard to lesser, and lesser to none). If the Strike hits, the meteor trail hangs in the air. This gives the benefits of concealment negation and cover reduction to any attacks made against the creature (by anyone) until the start of your next turn.

name: Skeletal Lancers
description:
You conjure a force of skeletons wielding bony spears. You create up to 5 thralls in different spaces within range. When an enemy makes a Strike while within 10 feet of a skeletal lancer, the lancer deals 5 piercing damage to it. The enemy takes this damage only once per Strike, even if it’s in the reach of multiple skeletal lancers. The skeletal lancers have a Speed of 30 feet. Their Strikes have a reach of 10 feet and deal piercing damage. When you command a skeletal lancer to Stride, you can have any number of your skeletal lancers Stride instead of just one. When you use thrall charge to order a skeletal lancer to make a Strike, that Strike deals an additional 2d6 damage.

Heightened (8th) The additional damage increases to 3d6.

name: Sky Sight
description: You gaze up and see the sky clearly despite environmental conditions. You can see through weather and physical obstructions such as a forest canopy, building material, and cave walls. This can be used to spot flying creatures or navigate by the stars even when you otherwise couldn’t see them.

name: Skyglass Prison
description:
The air around the target solidifies like glass, trapping the creature in a cage that perfectly encases them, making movement nearly impossible. A creature targeted with this spell must attempt a Fortitude save. The cage has AC 10, Hardness 5, and 30 Hit Points, and it’s immune to critical hits and precision damage. When a creature Escapes or the cage is destroyed, shards of hardened air cut the target creature, dealing 3d4 slashing damage. You can Dismiss this spell to destroy the cage.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is immobilized until it Escapes or until the cage is destroyed. The cage is automatically destroyed at the start of your next turn.

Failure The target is immobilized until it Escapes or until the cage is destroyed.

Critical Failure The target is restrained until it Escapes or until the cage is destroyed.

Heightened (+1) The cage’s Hit Points increase by 10, and the slashing damage increases by 1d4.

name: Sonata Span
description: By playing a brief tune on an instrument or in song, you cause the notes of the melody to physically manifest into a shimmering, translucent path. This path doesn’t need to be over solid ground and can tilt up or down diagonally up to 45 degrees, but it must be a straight, 5-foot-wide line. It can support as many creatures as can physically fit on the bridge.

name: Song of the Soul
description:
You shape a thrall into an instrument that plays a silent song that can be heard by only one soul. Choose one living or undead creature of your choice within 15 feet of the target thrall. That creature regains 1d8 Hit Points immediately and gains fast healing 1 for as long as it’s within 15 feet of the target thrall. This spell has the vitality trait if you heal a living creature or the void trait if you choose an undead creature.

Heightened (+1) The healing increases by 1d8 and the fast healing increases by 1.

name: Soothing Blossoms
description:
Blossoms grow from the ground in a small area, soothing away afflictions and persistent pains and harm. When any creature in that area rolls a successful save against a poison or disease effect, it gets a critical success instead. The blossoms grant assisted recovery to everyone in the area to end their persistent damage, both when the spell is cast and at the start of each of your turns.

Once the duration ends, the flowers lose their magical effect, but a few of them might survive in the area as long as they can naturally. This spell doesn’t give a benefit on a save against an affliction unless the stage lasts 10 minutes or less.

name: Soothing Spring
description:
Steam wisps into the air as a stone-lined pool appears in the ground and fills with hot water that bubbles up from the earth. The water is comfortably hot and smells mildly sulfurous in a not-unpleasant way. You can draw out the full energizing potential of the mineral-rich water. Any creature that spends the full hour soaking in the hot spring or basking in the mud from the bottom of the pit regains 10d8 Hit Points and feels refreshed, losing the fatigued condition. As normal for effects that remove fatigue, this doesn’t remove any underlying source of fatigue, such as lack of sleep, causing the condition to return if the underlying source isn’t addressed.

The pool is 20 feet on each side, and it’s 5 feet deep. It can contain 16 Medium or smaller creatures at a time. A Large creature counts as four Medium creatures, but a Huge creature fills the entire pool. This pool has the structure trait and the same restrictions as magic items that create structures.

Heightened (+1) The healing increases by 2d8.

name: Soul Cutter
description:
You conjure a blade of spiritual energy and cut at the soul of a foe. Make a melee spell attack against your target’s AC. On a success, you deal spirit damage. On a critical success, the target takes double damage. The number of actions you spend when Casting this Spell determines the range, damage, and other parameters. [single action] An adjacent target takes 3d6 spirit damage. [two actions] An adjacent target takes 6d6 spirit damage, and on a hit, it becomes enfeebled 1 for 1 round. [three actions] The blade flies out from you and attacks a target within 30 feet, dealing 6d6 spirit damage. The spell deals half damage on a failure (but not a critical failure), as the blade’s divine influence guides your attack. Unless you critically fail, the target becomes enfeebled 1 for 1 round.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d6 for the 1-action version, or by 2d6 for the 2-and 3-action versions.

name: Space Fold Gate
description:
You manipulate the fabric of space-time, temporarily bringing two distant points together, connected by a magical gate. Choose two unoccupied 5-foot squares on solid ground that you can see within range. You create spherical portals in both squares that are 5 feet tall and 5 feet wide connecting the two locations. Any creature that enters one portal can immediately transport itself to the exit portal as a part of its move action, which adds the teleportation trait to its movement (this movement still triggers reactions as normal). Physical objects can pass through the portal normally, as though the portals were adjacent. Ranged attacks made through the portals treat them as only one 5-foot square for the purpose of calculating range. Spells cast through the portals have no effect.

Heightened (6th) Range increases to 500 feet, and the portals can be made up to 10 feet tall and 10 feet wide.

Heightened (7th) Range increases to 1,000 feet, and the portals can be made up to 30 feet tall and 30 feet wide.

name: Speak with Magic
description:
You can ask questions of, receive answers from, and use the Diplomacy skill with spells and magic items of the same tradition used to Cast this Spell, or that have the magical trait and no tradition trait. When you do, your voice drops into a strange, ethereal register, and you speak a language that resembles a more fundamental version of Draconic. Speak with magic doesn’t make them more friendly than normal. Though magic isn’t intelligent, you speak with the essence of the spell or magic item, which has a personality colored by the type of effect and its purpose as well as by the caster of the spell or creator of the item. A spell or magic item’s perspective, perception, and knowledge give it a worldview different enough from a human’s that it doesn’t consider the same details important. They can mostly answer questions about their creator or caster, creatures that possessed or interacted with them in the past, and what the purpose of their magic is.

Heightened (4th) You can ask questions of, receive answers from, and use the Diplomacy skill with spells and magic items of any tradition.

Heightened (6th) As 4th rank, and the duration is 8 hours.

name: Speak with Water
description:
Using ancient magic, you shape the words you speak into the primal sounds of water. You can ask questions of and receive answers from a body of water or the rain. While water isn’t intelligent, you speak with the natural spirits within the water, which have a personality colored by the type of water as well as the activity and movement of the water. Water’s perspective, perception, and knowledge give it a worldview different enough from a human’s that it doesn’t consider the same details important. Rain is fleeting and knows only what it’s currently touching. It can direct you toward unique silhouettes or structures or find a hidden place under a city as rain washes through the sewers. A body of water’s perspective is shaped by its size and age. A lake might remember when a fisherman drowned within them, but the ocean will likely only recall the most significant of events, such as a city sinking beneath their waves.

Heightened (7th) The duration is 8 hours.

name: Spectral Blade
description:
You conjure a spectral throwing blade that always returns to your hand. You throw the blade when you Cast this Spell and the first time you Sustain this spell on subsequent turns, making a ranged spell attack against the AC of a creature within 20 feet. On a hit, you deal 3d6 spirit damage (or double damage on a critical hit). These attacks ignore any circumstance bonuses the target has to AC.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d6.

name: Spiked Carapace
description:
Your bones harmlessly puncture the skin of one arm, growing to form a hardened spiked gauntlet that can be used for both offense and defense. Make a melee spell attack against a target’s AC, dealing 5d8 piercing damage and 1d8 persistent bleed damage (double damage on a critical hit). You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your AC for the duration, as you deflect attacks with the gauntlet.

Heightened (+2) The initial damage increases by 2d8 and persistent bleed damage increases by 1d8.

name: Spinning Staff
description: You spin your staff with an impossibly quick twirling flourish, attacking two foes and transforming the momentum into magical energy to charge for your next Spellstrike. Make a melee Strike with your staff against one foe and then a second melee Strike with your staff against a different foe. Your multiple attack penalty applies to both of these attacks as normal.

name: Spontaneous Cartography
description:
Memory alone isn’t always sufficient for charting an area. You concentrate on a blank piece of parchment in your possession and record the landscape and geographical features within range. The resulting map bears crude but recognizable symbols to represent structures, landmarks, and pathways but doesn’t label them.

Heightened (6th) The range of this spell increases to 10 miles, and major landmarks are labeled. A small star shows the spot where you are when the map is created.

name: Stars of Another Sky
description:
You replace the sky with a mesmerizing vision of the Astral Plane’s River of Souls, pulling creatures toward their final destiny. You can Cast this Spell only if you’re outside. All creatures in the area must attempt a Will save, and they repeat the save each time you Sustain the spell.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected and temporarily immune to stars of another sky for 1 day.

Success The creature is fascinated by the beauty of the sky and rises 20 feet into the air. Creatures without a fly Speed remain in the air for the spell’s duration but fall when they recover from their fascinated condition. A creature that reaches the top of the cylinder doesn’t rise farther but takes 5d10 mental damage each time it starts its turn there due to a desire to become more immersed in the sky. Creatures without souls take double damage. If this damage drops the creature to 0 Hit Points, it dies instantly.

Failure As success, but the creature rises 50 feet into the air. Additionally, hostile actions don’t affect its fascinated condition for 1 round.

Critical Failure As failure, but the creature rises 100 feet into the air.

name: Stick On
description: The skin on your hand begins to ooze a strange adhesive that causes it to stick to a target. You and the target become inseparable for the spell’s duration or until the target Escapes. If the creature is smaller than you, it’s immobilized and pulled along with you as you move. If the target is the same size as you, you’re both pulled along with each other as either moves, but you both treat all spaces as difficult terrain. If the target is larger than you, you’re immobilized and pulled along as the target moves. You can Dismiss this spell.

name: Stop Heart
description:
With a cruel grasp, you reach into your opponent and squeeze at their heart. The target takes 10d10 void damage with a Fortitude save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target takes half damage and is sickened 1.

Failure The target takes full damage and is sickened 2.

Critical Failure The target takes double damage and is sickened 3.

Heightened (+1) The void damage increases by 1d10.

name: Sudden Swarm
description:
Sometimes, you need more allies to best you foes. Your familiar divides, turning into two familiars. Then they divide again, becoming four, then eight, and so on until there are innumerable copies of your familiar bustling about, eager to join the fight. While in its swarm form, your familiar gains immunity to precision damage and to the grappled, prone, and restrained conditions; weakness 4 to area and splash damage; and resistance 4 to piercing and slashing damage. It occupies the space of a Large creature and can occupy the same space as other creatures. If your familiar is reduced to 0 Hit Points while under the effect of this spell, the spell immediately ends, and your familiar is instead reduced to 1 Hit Point. Once per turn, your familiar can use the Swarming Bites action.

Swarming Bites [single action] Each creature in the familiar swarm’s space takes 3d6 damage of the appropriate type (basic Reflex save). Usually this is piercing damage, but depending on your familiar, it can be bludgeoning or slashing at the GM’s discretion.

Upon Casting this spell, you immediately Command your familiar. The first time each round you Sustain this spell on subsequent turns, you Command your familiar as part of the same action.

Heightened (+1) The damage of Swarming Bites increases by 1d6, and all resistances and weaknesses increase by 1.

name: Summoner's Precaution
description: Conjuring an intricate weave of protective magic, you create a buffer in the link between yourself and your eidolon, allowing your bonded ally to sacrifice their existence to save you in a time of need. You gain the following reaction; after using it, the spell ends. Sever Conduit [reaction] (concentrate) Trigger Your eidolon takes damage that would bring you to 0 Hit Points and comes from an effect other than a death effect; Effect You quickly extinguish the link with your eidolon, causing your bonded ally to wink out of existence before you can be laid low. Your eidolon unmanifests, and you can’t Manifest your Eidolon for 1 minute. In exchange, you don’t take the triggering damage, though your eidolon still suffers any other adverse effects that accompanied the damage.

name: Summoner's Visage
description:
No one understands you more than your eidolon and vice versa. Using this innate understanding, you transform your eidolon into your identical twin, allowing them to hide their presence or impersonate you to a limited extent. Assuming you’re a humanoid, the eidolon gains the humanoid trait in addition to their other traits while they’re in this form as well as any other trait related to your form (such as elf or gnome). Your eidolon gains a +4 status bonus to Deception checks to Impersonate you and can add their level to such checks even if they’re untrained.

Although your eidolon looks like you, they don’t gain any new abilities, and their statistics don’t change in any way— the transformation is purely cosmetic. If this transformation reduces your eidolon’s size, the eidolon loses any other effects of their larger size, such as any increase to reach. Your eidolon can still use gear only if it has the eidolon trait, which allows eidolons to use it. If necessary, any such eidolon items the eidolon was wearing remain active but change size and shape to reflect what you’re wearing. You can Dismiss this spell to return your eidolon to their original form.

Heightened (4th) The duration increases to 1 hour.

name: Synchronize
description:
You harmlessly place your unique magic sigil in the shape of your choice, which is about 1 square inch in size, on your targets. When you Cast the Spell, you set the duration by choosing a time at which point the sigil flashes dimly three times. After that point, the spell ends. Even though spell durations aren’t normally exact, the effects of synchronize are precise to the second. The timer is based on the place where the spell was cast, so entering a plane or area where time flows differently changes how the time elapses in sometimes unpredictable ways.

Heightened (2nd) The spell can target up to 20 willing creatures.

name: Tacky Pine Sap
description:
You conjure highly flammable pine sap, covering the area with it. This area becomes difficult terrain. When a creature within the area uses a fire effect or receives fire damage, the sap ignites, dealing 1d6 persistent fire damage to anyone standing on it; this burns up the sap, removing it and its difficult terrain.

Heightened (+2) The persistent fire damage increases by 1d6.

name: Tame
description:
As you make comforting sounds and gestures, you approach the target in a friendly manner combining caution and confidence. You improve the target’s attitude to you by one step (unfriendly to neutral, neutral to friendly, friendly to helpful) for the duration of the spell unless it succeeds at a Will save. Afterward, the target is temporarily immune for 1 day.

This spell works only on domesticated animals; for example, you could use it on guard dogs or stray dogs but not feral dogs or wolves. If the socialization of the animal is in question, the decision is up to the GM.

Heightened (3rd) The duration becomes 10 minutes.

Heightened (6th) The duration becomes 1 hour.

name: Tear the Veil
description:
You cause the barrier between the Universe and the Void to weaken as waves of void energy pull the living toward the tear to their inevitable doom. The area is difficult terrain to all living creatures. When you Cast this Spell and the first time each round you Sustain it on subsequent rounds, all living creatures in the area must attempt a Fortitude saving throw.

Critical Success The target is unaffected. Success The target takes 5d12 void damage and is pulled 15 feet toward the center. Failure The target takes 10d12 void damage and is pulled 30 feet toward the center. Critical Failure The target takes 20d12 void damage and is pulled 30 feet toward the center.

There’s an additional 5-foot burst in the center of the area that drains the life away from all who touch it. Whenever a living creature begins its turn in this burst, it becomes drained 1, or its drained condition increases by 1 to a maximum of drained 4. A target that is drained 4 and begins its turn in the center burst must attempt a Fortitude save that has the death and incapacitation traits; on a failure, it is reduced to 0 Hit Points, crumbles into ash, and becomes a wraith. The gear of the creature that’s transformed in this way falls to the ground in its space.

name: Temporary Possession
description:
You destroy the target thrall, using its destruction as a catalyst to temporarily possess an enemy. One living or undead target creature within 15 feet of the destroyed thrall must attempt a Will saving throw.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is controlled by you until the end of your turn, and you can have it take up to one action of your choice: Drop Prone, Interact, Release what it’s holding, or Strike. The possessed creature’s Strikes use and contribute toward your multiple attack penalty. At the end of your turn, the creature is no longer controlled and becomes stunned 1. If the creature loses any Hit Points for any reason while it’s possessed or stunned by this ability, you lose Hit Points equal to half that amount since your spirit partially lingers within its body.

Failure As success, but you can spend up to 2 actions.

Critical Failure As success, but you can spend up to 3 actions.

name: Tentacular Innervation
description:
One of your limbs blisters and your muscles extend to create a nestling assemblage of tentacles. This visceral mass is a short-lived magical parasite that seeks to connect to an unfortunate foe’s nervous system. Make an unarmed melee Strike. Your reach increases by 10 feet for this Strike. If the Strike hits, in addition to dealing its normal damage, the target becomes sickened 1 and is grabbed by the mass of tentacles. The target isn’t immobilized, but it can’t move beyond the reach of the unarmed melee Strike that has grabbed it. If the target Escapes from the mass of tentacles (using your spell DC as the Escape DC), the spell ends. The mass of tentacles can be severed before the spell’s duration ends; it has AC 10 and 60 Hit Points, and it’s immune to critical hits and precision damage.

Heightened (+1) The Hit Points of the tentacles increases by 10.

name: The Everfull Moon
description:
A Linnorm King once defended her kingdom from Irriseni invaders with a casting of this spell. You call upon the secret moon, who's always whole, to shine upon yourself, granting you the form of a mighty werewolf without letting the curse touch you. You transform yourself into a Large hybrid wolf battle form. While in this form, you gain the beast trait. This battle form doesn't prevent you from speaking, casting spells, or using your hands. You gain the following abilities. AC = 18 + your level. Ignore your armor's check penalty and Speed reduction.A +1 status bonus to saving throws.20 temporary Hit Points.Darkvision and scent as an imprecise sense with a range of 30 feet.Your proficiency bonus equals your level for untrained skill checks using Acrobatics or Athletics.The claw and jaws unarmed melee attacks detailed below. You're trained with them, your attack modifier is +10, and you use the listed damage. These attacks are Strength based (for the purpose of the enfeebled condition, for example). If your unarmed attack modifier is higher, you can use it instead.Melee [single action] jaws (reach), Damage 2d8 piercing.Melee [single action] claw (agile, reach), Damage 2d6 slashing.Speed of 40 feet, unless your own is higher.When you Fuel The Everfull Moon, you gain 20 temporary Hit Points.

Lethologic Mark During any night that isn't the new moon, you gain a weakness to silver equal to your level. The mark is healed if you become a true werewolf and become cured of said curse.

Heightened (+2) The temporary Hit Points granted by this spell when you cast or Fuel it increase by 20. All unarmed Strikes granted by this spell deal an additional die of damage. Your attack modifier increases by +6. Finally, your AC increases by 2.

name: Theogeny
description: You spark the genesis of a new divine realm around you. The appearance of the area becomes more obviously divine, matching your own beliefs. All creatures within the area temporarily transcend into divine beings. If you’re holy, your allies gain the holy trait, while your foes gain the unholy trait and weakness 5 to holy. Similarly, if you’re unholy, your allies gain the unholy trait, while your foes gain the holy trait and weakness 5 to unholy. Creatures that already have the holy or unholy trait don’t gain any new traits or weaknesses. While in the area, you and all allies gain a fly Speed equal to their highest Speed, and their Strikes gain the sanctified trait and deal an additional 1d10 spirit damage on hit. Additionally, all enemies take 10 spirit damage whenever they’re critically hit by an attack or whenever they critically fail a saving throw.

name: Thicket of Knives
description: You create numerous phantom copies of your weapon arm, hiding your true movements and rendering your attacks unpredictable. You gain a +2 status bonus to Deception checks. If you’re untrained in Deception, you can use the Feint action anyway as well as add your level as your proficiency bonus despite being untrained.

name: Thrall Charge
description:
You urge a thrall to move and attack. You command the target thrall to Stride and then make a Strike that deals an additional 1d6 damage. You can destroy the thrall as part of this Strike to add a status bonus to the Strike’s damage equal to this spell’s rank.

Heightened (2nd) The additional damage increases to 2d6.

Heightened (6th) The additional damage increases to 3d6.

Heightened (10th) The additional damage increases to 4d6.

name: Thunder Echo
description: With a clap of your hands, you emit a loud but harmless burst of electricity, interpreting the discharged electrostatic sparks to navigate the area and help reveal secrets. Hidden chambers, objects, and creatures within the area of the effect become easier to find as they spark with static electricity, causing all creatures to gain a +2 status bonus to Perception checks to locate them for the duration. The area of effect is unimpeded by walls and solid objects.

name: Thundering Dominance
description:
You shroud the target in a powerful predatory aura and amplify its vocalizations. It gains a +1 status bonus to Intimidation checks. Once during this spell’s duration, it can take the Thundering Roar action. Thundering Roar [single action] (auditory, concentrate, emotion, fear, mental, sonic) The target unleashes a powerful vocalization. Each enemy in a 10-foot emanation takes 4d8 sonic damage with a basic Will save against your spell DC. A creature that fails its Will save is also frightened 1.

Heightened (+2) The status bonus to Intimidation checks increases by 1 (to a maximum of a +4 status bonus for an 8th-rank spell), and the damage from Thundering Roar increases by 2d8.

name: Thunderous Strike
description:
You swing your massive weapon, creating a wave of sonic vibrations that topples creatures. Make a melee Strike with your two-handed weapon. Each creature in a 15-foot cone from you must attempt a basic Fortitude save against your spell DC or take 2 sonic damage. On a critical failure, the creature is knocked prone. The target of your Strike must be within the cone or the effect fails.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1.

name: Time Jump
description:
You leap through time, appearing across the battlefield in the blink of an eye. You gain 2 actions, each of which must be used to Leap, Stand, Step, or Stride. If you have an appropriate Speed, you can add Burrow, Climb, Fly, or Swim to this list.

While you take these actions, time pauses. All other creatures are completely unaware of your actions, can’t speak, and can’t use any actions that would be triggered by your movement. While you’re taking these actions, you can’t take any other actions, including any that would be triggered by the move actions. Once the actions are complete, time starts again, and to onlookers, you seem to have suddenly teleported across the distance you traveled. Leaping forward through time is disorienting, so if you use time jump again within 1 minute of using the spell, you become stupefied 4 for 1 minute.

name: Timely Reminder
description:
You send a message to yourself that’s delivered at a delayed time of your choosing. Whisper a message no longer than 8 words and concentrate on a date and time within the next year. At the chosen moment, a gentle chime will sound in your head, followed by the message repeated twice in an average, steady tone. This spell can be Dismissed at any time. If a new casting of timely reminder is used, the first message is erased as soon as the new message is created.

Heightened (5th) You send the reminder message to another willing creature you know. If the creature isn’t on the same plane of existence when you Cast this Spell, the spell fails.

name: Timely Tutor
description:
You serve as an astral connection between your eidolon or familiar and the Akashic Record—a demiplane consisting of a comprehensive psychic library. If you Cast this Spell on your familiar, your familiar adds your spellcasting attribute modifier on checks to Recall Knowledge with the Lore skill of your choice, much like they do for Acrobatics and Stealth. Your familiar must have the speech familiar ability in order to share any information they learn with you. If you Cast this Spell on your eidolon, they instead become trained in the Lore skill of your choice.

If you lose physical contact with the target, their connection to the Akashic Record is severed, and the spell immediately ends.

name: Tiny Wings
description:
You hold your familiar in your arms and then throw them into the sky—whereupon they sprout wings and take flight. The wings look appropriate to the familiar’s nature. A tabby cat might simply grow a pair of grayish wings like a pigeon, while a frog grows membranous wings a bit like a bat. Your familiar gains a 20-foot fly Speed.

Familiars who already have a fly Speed instead gain a +15-foot status bonus to their fly Speed.

name: Tornadic Gale
description:
A spinning gale of violent air bursts forth from you, drawing creatures into its vortex. All Medium or smaller creatures that are adjacent to the line are pulled to the nearest unoccupied space within the line. Then, all creatures within the line take 5d12 bludgeoning damage and must attempt a Reflex save.

Critical Success The target takes no damage.

Success The target takes half damage.

Failure The target takes full damage and is pushed 5 feet away from you.

Critical Failure The target takes double damage, is pushed 10 feet away from you, and is knocked prone.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d12.

name: Tortoise and the Hare
target: 1 foe, and either yourself or 1 ally
description:
You prove that slow and steady doesn’t always win the race by slowing a foe into a proverbial tortoise and yourself or an ally into a hare, siphoning some of the foe’s speed and granting it to the other target. The effects depend on the foe’s Fortitude save.

Critical Success The targets are unaffected.

Success The foe is slowed 1 for 1 round, and the other target is unaffected.

Failure The foe is slowed 1 for 3 rounds, and the other target is quickened for 1 round. They can use the extra action only to Step, Stride, or Strike.

Critical Failure The foe is slowed 1 for 3 minutes, and the other target is quickened for 1 minute. They can use the extra action only to Step, Stride, or Strike.

name: Tracing Bond
description: You and an ally might be parting ways, but you know that you’ll continue to have each other’s backs. For the duration of the spell, you and the ally always know the direction and distance to the other’s location as long as you’re both on the same plane of existence. While this bond doesn’t allow you to send messages or generally know the other person’s status, at any point during the spell, either of you can send a single distress signal to the other as a single action that has the concentrate and mental traits. This signal is a simple mental alert that doesn’t provide any additional details about the situation or status of the person. Once this signal has been used, neither target can send another signal for the duration of the spell.

name: Tracking Mayflies
description: You shape a magical swarm of ephemeral mayflies, which direct your shot as it soars through the sky. Make a ranged Strike. For this Strike, double your weapon’s range increment. If the target is under the effect of a spell, is wielding a magic item, or is wearing a magic item, it’s off-guard against this Strike, as the mayflies become increasingly unpredictable when hunting a source of magic. If the target was invisible, the target becomes concealed to this Strike instead. If the target was already concealed for any other reason, it’s no longer concealed to this Strike. If the Strike is successful, the target is dazzled for 1 round as the mayflies swarm around the target’s face.

name: Tree of Life and Death
description:
The cycle of life includes both life and death, growth and decay. You call forth two mighty trees from the depths of the Boneyard, one emanating with life and one with death, bound to each other as the living are to the dying. The trees must be at least 20 feet apart. Each one occupies its square, and its canopy spreads out in a 10-foot emanation. Each tree has AC 10, Hardness 10, and 50 Hit Points. They’re immune to critical hits and precision damage. When either tree is reduced to 0 Hit Points or the spell ends, both trees disintegrate into a pile of dust.

  • Tree of Death Charred branches cover the tree, and the area of its emanation fills with a foul miasma. A living creature that starts its turn within or enters the emanation takes 5d4 void damage, with a basic Fortitude save. A creature can only be damaged this way once per round.
  • Tree of Life Golden leaves cover the tree, and the area of its emanation fills with shining particles. A living creature that starts its turn within or enters the emanation regains 5d4 Hit Points. A creature can only be healed this way once per round.

Heightened (+1) The void damage increases by 1d4, the healing increases by 1d4, and tree’s Hit Points increases by 10.

name: Unbounded Sphere
description:
You magically desynchronize the current plane of existence, trapping creatures in an area that loops back on itself in the manner of an unbounded plane. Whenever a creature attempts to enter or leave the area, they must attempt a Will saving throw.

Critical Success The creature moves into or out of the area as intended.

Success The creature moves into or out of the area successfully but appears it a random unoccupied space adjacent to the edge of the area.

Failure The creature fails to enter or exit the area, instead appearing at a random, unoccupied space adjacent to the edge of the area, and their movement immediately ends.

Critical Failure As failure, except the creature can’t attempt to enter or leave again this turn.

name: Uncover Device
description: You focus on the construction of the object, channeling electricity through it that allows you to get a sense of its shape and construction. You gain a +2 status bonus to Thievery checks to Disable Device on the target and to Aid checks to help an ally Disable Devise on the target.

name: Under Sunless Skies
description:
A long-forgotten army in the Darklands attempted to clinch a crucial battle by blacking out the sun with an impossible spell. The sun goes dark across the entire area of the spell, manipulating your enemies and giving your allies great resilience. The spell’s area comes under a 9th-rank darkness spell. You and all allies in the area gain greater darkvision, 40 temporary Hit Points, and a +3 status bonus to saving throws for the spell’s duration. Enemies within the area take a –3 status penalty to Will saving throws. Whenever you Fuel Under Sunless Skies, you cast a 9th-rank command spell without expending a spell slot, targeting all enemies within the area. You must give the same command to all enemies.

Lethologic Mark Your sight becomes easily affected by light. When first exposed to bright light, you become blinded until the end of your next turn. After this exposure, light doesn't blind you again until after you spend 1 hour in darkness. To heal this mark, you must drink a potion created with a vial of black blood created by the Groetan hags of the Sightless Sea.

name: Unexpected Transposition
target: 1 creature other than the triggering enemy
description: When attacked, you attempt to quickly swap your own position with that of another creature, causing them to get hit in your place. A creature that’s unwilling to swap places with you must attempt a Will save. Willing creatures automatically fail, and you switch places. If you successfully switch places with the target, the triggering attack is resolved against that creature as if it had been the original target of the attack. After the swap, you and the target are both temporarily immune to unexpected transposition spells for 1 minute.

name: Unfetter Eidolon
description: You loosen the link between yourself and your eidolon, allowing them to travel farther from you for a short period of time and aiding them against being immobilized. While the spell is active, your eidolon can travel an unlimited distance away from you and gains a +1 status bonus to saving throws and DCs against any effect that would make them grappled, immobilized, or restrained, plus the Reposition and Swallow Whole actions. When the spell ends, if your eidolon is more than 100 feet away from you, they unmanifest.

name: Unravel Existence
description:
You disturb a section of reality itself, tearing creatures apart at a fundamental level using your current plane of existence as fuel. When you Cast this Spell and the first time you Sustain it on subsequent rounds, each creature in the area takes 5d10 force damage with a basic Fortitude save. On a failed save, a creature that isn’t a native inhabitant of the plane also takes 1d10 persistent force damage and becomes off-guard until it recovers from this persistent damage. A target reduced to 0 Hit Points by either damage scatters into fine dust; its gear remains.

Heightened (+2) The initial and persistent force damage increases by 1d10.

name: Unrelenting Gravity
description:
Even the fundamental forces of the universe can bend to your magic and submit to your will. You create an isolated but powerful downward force by greatly increasing the force of gravity your target experiences, hampering its movement and pushing it to the ground. The target must attempt a Fortitude save.

Critical Success The target is unaffected.

Success The target is encumbered for 1 round.
